Fetish

FET-ish -- two syllables, stress on the first syllable, FET. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Fetish is an obsession, or an object believed to hold magical power.

The archaeologist catalogued a bone fetish that hunters once wore for luck.

Worked Example

In one museum case sits a small clay figure from a farming village: each spring it was carried to the fields, spoken to politely, and set facing the rain clouds, because the whole village believed the harvest depended on it.

That figure is a fetish in the word's original sense: an object believed to hold special or magical power. By extension, English also uses fetish for an unusual fixation -- caring about something far beyond what it seems to deserve, like a fetish for perfectly sharpened pencils.

How Fetish Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

talisman

talisman: a charm carried to bring its owner luck or protection; a fetish is itself revered, believed to house a spirit or power

obsession

obsession: an idea or thing someone cannot stop thinking about

fixation

fixation: an intense, locked-in focus on one thing

Antonyms

indifference

indifference: a complete lack of interest

aversion

aversion: a strong dislike that makes you avoid something

How Strong Is It? — fixation → fetish → obsession

fixation vs. fetish

fixation vs. fetish: A fixation locks attention on one thing, often temporarily, while a fetish goes further: the attention hardens into a ritual the person cannot easily set aside.

obsession vs. fetish

obsession vs. fetish: Obsession is the strongest of the three: a fetish for antique maps can still be a charming quirk, but an obsession crowds everything else out of a person's life.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — feitiço

root — feitiço: a charm, sorcery; a thing made by art (Portuguese feitiço, from Latin facticius 'made by art,' from facere 'to make')

Put it together

Put it together: Portuguese sailors used feitiço, 'a made thing, a charm,' for the carved objects they saw honored along the West African coast; the word traces back to Latin facere, 'to make.' A fetish is literally a made object -- made by hands, and made powerful by belief.

Word Choice

In this course, fetish carries two related senses: the anthropologist's sense -- an object believed to hold magical power, like a carved charm -- and the everyday sense of an unusual fixation ('a fetish for alphabetized bookshelves'). Both grow from the same idea: an object or habit granted far more power than it visibly deserves. On the ISEE, read the sentence to see which sense is in play.
